limits.sandbox: CPU-only Docker python@c61cffc3, no network, 256 MB, 1 CPU, 10 s per grade

scheduling.placement: agent j of case c on replica/grader host (c+j)%4
scheduling.concurrency_note: each arm alone on the fleet: 20 client requests per node <= 25

serving.launch: inkling/serve.sh with MEM=0.75 (cookbook dgx-spark/nvfp4/dspark + text-only, ctx 131072; KV pool ~1.08M tokens per node since 2026-11-21 16:25 Europe/Warsaw)
serving.adapter: inkling/shim.py (vLLM dialect; client disconnects are shim:client_cancels)

selection: the first proposal in TIME order that passes ALL feedback cases ends the case: other agents of the case are terminated, queued ones never start; solved if it passes ALL holdout cases
execution: Each arm alone on the fleet via inkling/coding_arms.py (fresh admission with shim sha and mem fraction 0.75, prefix-cache flush, server counters, idle wait, GPU energy). S first, then E.
exclusions: None; all 72 cases of each arm count.
resume_rule: As in earlier coding plans: on an operational fault the runner stops admissions; the same arm is continued only for unfinished cases with the same seeds and documented as an amendment.
frozen_note: Frozen 2026-11-21 before any call with seeds 7-9 on coding-hard-v1. Follow-up of coding-earlystop-v1 (early stop at the first proposal passing the public tests is the coding default: 69/72 at -37 % tokens vs running all 8). A replay of that run's full arm (aligned timeline, in-sample) predicted that starting 4 agents and adding the other 4 only if nothing has passed after 300 s keeps 70/72 at about -17 % tokens (55K vs 66K per case).
question: Does a staggered start (4 agents, 4 more only if no proposal passes the public tests within 300 s or all of the first four fail) keep the accuracy of the early-stop default with all 8 agents started at once, at fewer server tokens?

primary_outcomes.tokens: Server-counted generated tokens per case, S vs E.
primary_outcomes.accuracy: Solved/72, S vs E, paired two-sided exact sign test (contains run-to-run noise of a few cases).
primary_outcomes.wall: Arm wall time and median / p90 case stop time, S vs E.

decision_rule: The staggered start becomes the coding default if S server tokens per case <= 0.85 x E AND S solved >= E solved - 2 (noise allowance) AND S arm wall <= 1.10 x E. Otherwise E (all 8 at once with early stop) stays.
secondary_outcomes: GPU energy per solved case; cases where the second wave started (and why: 300 s or first wave failed); never-started agents; per-case stop times.
arm: E: early stop with all 8 agents queued at once (the coding default since coding-earlystop-v1)
smoke: Throwaway smoke (not part of the study) on development task dev-wrap_hyphen, seed 9, stagger first=2 after 60 s: agents 1-2 started at 0 s, agents 3-4 at +61 s, agent 1 passed the public tests at 147 s and the other three were terminated.
